verdict: APA's revenue fell 22% to $1.99B because last year's result included a $620M UK tax settlement gain; underlying production rose 4% and new Suriname oil started flowing.

kpis.label: Revenues
kpis.note: -22% vs a year ago (which had a $620M one-off gain)

kpis.label: EPS (diluted)
kpis.note: Vs $3.49 a year ago, on the flows shown

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: Free cash flow was $365M after capital spending

segments.name: United States
segments.note: Permian Basin shale. Lower oil and gas prices were offset by new production from the Granite Ridge merger.

segments.name: Egypt
segments.note: Western Desert production; volumes fell on natural decline.

segments.name: North Sea (UK)
segments.note: Maturing UK platforms; higher realized gas prices cushioned lower volumes.

segments.name: Suriname
segments.note: First full quarter of oil from the Gran Amatista field, which started up in June 2026.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Head-office and administrative costs; APA cut G&A 11% from a year ago.

opex.name: Exploration
opex.note: Dry holes and exploration write-offs, mainly in Egypt.

opex.name: Merger & separation
opex.note: Remaining costs of the Granite Ridge combination.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $120M, partly offset by a $64M gain as APA's stake in Granite Ridge rose in value and $9M of other income.

takeaways.title: Revenue fell to $1.99B
takeaways.text: Almost all of the drop is the absence of last year's $620M UK tax-settlement gain in the comparison, not weaker operations.

takeaways.title: Production rose to 488 Mboe/d
takeaways.text: Permian growth, the Granite Ridge merger and new Suriname output more than offset declines in Egypt and the North Sea, while realized gas prices fell sharply.

takeaways.title: EPS of $1.22 vs $3.49 a year ago
takeaways.text: Profit fell with the one-off gain gone and prices lower, though operating cash flow of $1.26B stayed strong. The growth bet is Suriname: a final investment decision on the larger GranMorgu project is expected in Q2 2027.

footerNote: Excluded from the flow above so the chart stays readable: a $333M provision for valuation allowances against Egyptian tax credits under APA's RightWay program (recorded in its own income-statement line), $248M of impairments of curtailed projects recorded inside lease operating expense, and $32M of restructuring charges recorded within the tax line, so income tax is shown as reported. Including all of these, APA's reported net income attributable to common stock was $22M (EPS $0.07). Net income shown is before $69M attributed to noncontrolling interests.
